data.title: Nepal floods explained: The chain of events behind the disaster
data.description: A glacier broke apart. An ice and rock avalanche followed. Then came an earthquake, before a landslide triggered devastating floods that tore through kilometres of valley. This is what happened along the Nepal-China border, where rescue teams are still trying to recover survivors 48 hours after the catastrophe. FRANCE 24 breaks down the chain of events and the scientific explanations behind the disaster.

data.title: Japan's controversial WWII heroes: How one kamikaze pilot escaped certain death
data.description: Towards the end of World War II, as US troops advanced across the Pacific, Japan resorted to a desperate strategy: kamikaze attacks. Thousands of Japanese pilots, with an average age of just 21, were ordered to crash their explosive-laden planes into enemy ships. More than 3,800 pilots gave up their lives, killing over 7,000 allied naval personnel. Our reporter Mélodie Sforza met one of the last surviving former kamikaze pilots.

data.title: Nepal flash floods: 'Very challenging' for survivors who have lost their homes and their families
data.description: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Sunita Sharma, Head of Programs of Karuna-Shechen. While Nepal has considerable experience responding to natural disasters, the scale of the present devastation exposes a deeper challenge: Placing greater emphasis on preparedness. The immediate priorities are clear: finding those still missing and providing survivors with drinking water, food, shelter, clothing and medicine. But recovery cannot end there. Ultimately, they will need to rebuild confidence and entire communities. Given the scale of the destruction, that process could take years.

data.title: El Niño, paired with climate change, 'just makes everything so much more dangerous'
data.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Gareth Redmond-King, Head of the International Programme at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit. He warns we are entering a period in which climate change is not only intensifying extreme weather but adding greater instability to the climate system itself. Natural phenomena such as El Niño will then amplify, and intensify, that disruption, effectively “fanning the flames of climate change” and making already dangerous extremes even more severe. For Europe, this means that the extreme heat, drought, water shortages, storms and flash flooding we are experiencing should no longer be regarded as exceptional. They are increasingly part of a new normal for which governments remain inadequately prepared.

data.title: ‘I don’t care if I look good’: French heartthrob Louis Garrel on fashion, fatherhood and his radically dorky new role
data.description: The star has long been French cinema’s favourite tousle-haired Adonis, which makes his latest performance – as a schlubby, stay-at-home dad – all the more surprising. ‘I appreciate people laughing at me,’ he says ‘Even though I’ve been working in film for over 20 years, I still have this desire to look beautiful on screen,” says Louis Garrel, on a video call from his bed inside a boat off the coast of Corsica. The French film star is lying on his stomach, occasionally kicking up his bare legs, ruffling his curls and running the nail of his thumb over his moustache. I think the person he sees on the laptop screen in front of him is me, but I am pretty certain he is flirting with his own reflection. The attraction between the Paris-born 43-year-old and the camera tends to be reciprocal. Long of limb, tousled of hair and chiselled of nose, Garrel has spent a career on screen as French cinema’s favourite Adonis – the man film-makers turn to when they need an erotic wrecking ball to smash up bourgeois twosomes and turn them into quivering menages a trois. data.title: Bigmouth strums again: was Andy Burnham’s Smiths jam in Kyiv the perfect soundtrack to a Britain in freefall?
data.description: The UK prime minister clearly still adores the band. Perhaps he’s attracted to songs about sham justice and murderous meat factories, shot through with nihilism and exquisite despair As an origin story, Andy Burnham: Smiths Fan has a lot going for it. It’s plainly authentic: he can name the time he saw them live (Salford University, Queen Is Dead tour, 1986). A cynical young man in a hurry might fake that now, but not back when he first said it, in 2013. Asked by Labour Uncut for his desert island tracks during his 2010 leadership bid, three of the eight were sung by Morrissey (two Smiths singles and one off Viva Hate), which is superfan territory. That’s a softball exercise to endear yourself to Labour members; you have eight chances to hit every base, and to blow three lives on an artist who had already, by then, been dabbling in nationalism for 18 years (we’ll come back to this) was dicey and brave. You’ll recall that Burnham did not win that election. If you were an enemy state, amassing this hinterland for an asset, you’d have basically done a really good job. Continue reading...

data.title: From maligned second city to Insta magnet: Marseille is France’s new capital of overtourism | Mary Fitzgerald
data.description: This summer has been a tipping point. But it’s not too late to save what makes this place unique When I first started visiting Marseille more than 20 years ago, few could have predicted that France’s then beleaguered second city would become one of the most popular destinations in the most-visited country in the world . Tarnished by stereotypes and home to some of Europe’s most disadvantaged neighbourhoods, the port city seemed down on its luck, unloved and, in the eyes of many, somewhere to avoid. Tourists stopping at the city’s Saint-Charles station would clutch their bags while waiting for their connecting train to rural Provence, or the beaches of the Côte d’Azur. Two decades on, poverty and drug gang violence still affect parts of Marseille, but this rough diamond has been reinvented as a modish holiday destination. Last month, I saw a local TV channel asking whether Marseille had become France’s capital of tourism , after Booking.com revealed it had surpassed Paris and Nice as the most searched-for destination for French users of the site. Breathless foreign media coverage – the New York Times published a “36 hours in Marseille” guide in 2019 and another one in 2025 – has driven the number of overseas visitors. From seaside petanque to vocoder rap and pizza served on aluminium plates, influencers revel in the golden-hued aesthetic of the urban riviera and promote the city’s most Instagram-friendly corners. Tourist numbers are expected to reach almost 7 million this year . Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m an ever-changing vessel’: Erykah Badu on defying definition, life as a birth and death doula and her first album in 11 years
data.description: Why do the Texan innovator’s records take so long to make? ‘It’s important to gather the data,’ she says: the death, dating and dopamine behind her exquisite comeback alongside the Alchemist Erykah Badu needs the lights down low . The singer, producer, actor and registered doula shuffles into a private room at London’s Soho hotel and quietly asks for some changes to the atmosphere: lights dimmed, soft seat. A green juice would be great. As it turns out, Badu was out last night with Dave Chappelle, sitting with the comedian at a grand piano and playing songs into the wee hours. She looks mischievous when she thinks about the impromptu party, but declines to go into detail about what, exactly, went on. Instead, the 55-year-old smiles at me, eyes wide, her gold teeth glinting in the low light: “Oh yes,” she says slowly and quietly, like some kind of mysterious warlock. “It was a late one …” Continue reading...

data.title: How Katseye became the world’s biggest girl group – while falling apart
data.description: Their raucous pop music has made Katseye the biggest girl band in two decades. Can they weather toxic fandom, critical pans and a dwindling member count? Before screenings of their new documentary, the members of Katseye appear in a video message to thank fans for their support. Their followers, Eyekons, have played a critical role in their rise to stardom, so it makes sense that Katseye: Wild Hearts , released in global theaters this month, takes a beat to shout out to them. Perhaps more than many other big music groups today, the group’s rise has depended on their relationship with their devotees who ensure that few corners of the world are safe from Katseye mania. Katseye’s multinational members – Daniela, Lara, Manon, Megan, Sophia and Yoonchae – were selected through a combination of fan votes and judge scores on the 2023 YouTube reality competition The Debut: Dream Academy. The joint project between American record label Geffen Records and Korean entertainment company Hybe aimed to create a global girl group, with hopefuls participating in a rigorous bootcamp to test their singing and dancing skills. The following year, Netflix’s docu-series Pop Star Academy: Katseye – which documented the group’s nascent era, behind-the-scenes drama and all – catapulted them to a new level of visibility. data.title: Sweetener used in chewing gum and jam linked to strokes and heart attacks

data.title: The Guide #258: the perennially puerile, eternally eccentric Adult Swim turns 25
data.description: In this week’s newsletter: resolutely for grownups but proudly immature, the late-night channel has influenced an entire genre of comedy. But it still retains its cult status • Don’t get The Guide delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Twenty five years ago this coming week, a strange block of programming suddenly began airing in the wee small hours on the US cable channel Cartoon Network. Anyone half-watching with the sound off might have mistaken the shows as a continuation of the toons airing in the daytime: bright, big-eyed affairs full of energy and slapstick comedy. Those paying attention, though, would have noticed something was off: old-fashioned Hanna-Barbera superheroes had been recast as attorneys or talkshow hosts ; a crew of talking fast-food items, supposedly a hero squad called the Aqua Teen Hunger Force , just seemed to be bickering with each other and watching TV rather than fighting crime; and the whole mood of the programmes, with their halting, babbled dialogue, juvenile humour and janky animation, seemed not quite right. The name of the block was odd too: Adult Swim . Piggybacking on the adult animation boom of the 90s – The Simpsons, South Park et al. – Adult Swim steered things off in to bizarre and unsettling new territory. If anything, it’s only gotten weirder in the quarter of a century since it started. Close to 100 shows have aired in this insomnia-friendly night-time block (though today it arguably operates as its own independent channel within a channel), almost all of them strange enough to make you feel like you might be asleep after all and having a particularly psychedelic dream. It has platformed demon-fighting death metal bands , redneck squids , preposterously dark claymation parodies of Rankin/Bass , and a crime-fighting, gun-toting backside – as well as real-life figures with faces as boggle-eyed and elasticated as their cartoon counterparts. It has remained a defiant corner of freakery in a homogenised TV landscape. Continue reading...

data.title: Choking is sold to teens as a safe sexual practice. The research says it never is
data.description: More and more young people are engaging in sexual strangulation. But experts say there’s no safe pressure – and we have to start talking to teenagers about it When touching someone’s throat, it can only take the pressure of a handshake to cause serious injury, unconsciousness or death. These injuries, which include brain damage and stroke, are often internal and invisible, showing up days or even months after the initial incident occurred. Experts say many who participate in sexual choking are not aware of the risks. Choking or sexual strangulation is common among young people, says Prof Heather Douglas of the Melbourne Law School. In a 2024 survey of 4,702 Australians aged between 18 and 35, she and her research team found that 57% reported ever having experienced sexual strangulation; 51% reported ever having strangled a partner and 43.9% reported participating in both. Continue reading...

data.title: The chefs turning down the heat by switching from gas to electric
data.description: As well as being quieter, cheaper to run and easier to clean, induction cookers can cut kitchen temperatures by up to 10C Leaping flames, searing heat, copious sweat and scorchingly inventive swearing – restaurant kitchens are never a place for the faint-hearted, but this summer they have been sweltering in successive heatwaves to a dangerous degree. Some restaurants, cafes and bakeries in the UK grew so hot that they were forced to close , or reduce their hours , for the safety of their staff. There is still no maximum working temperature, despite calls from the TUC , and tens of thousands of kitchen staff are thought to have carried on working in “furnace-like” conditions . data.title: Memo to Ridley Scott: no one needs more Alien: Covenant movies – get the franchise back to stalk’n’slash
data.description: News that Scott is working on a follow-up to his maligned 2017 film leaves me worried the franchise has run out of shocks If any science-fiction saga looked beyond recovery, it was the Alien franchise. For the 38 years that followed James Cameron’s Aliens, film-makers contrived to find every imaginable way of not making a good Alien film. They tried killing everyone the audience cared about before the opening credits, marooning Sigourney Weaver on a planet populated entirely by bald British character actors , cloning Ripley , pitting xenomorphs against Predators , and sending scientists across the universe to ask an enormous, hairless space bodybuilder why he made them . They even ponied up the thick end of $100m for a film in which Michael Fassbender teaches himself to play the flute . And then in 2024, we got Fede Álvarez’s Alien: Romulus , in which actual xenomorphs chase actual human beings down actual corridors for the clearly defined purposes of either killing them or putting smaller xenomorphs inside them. Better still, a year later we got Noah Hawley’s Alien: Earth , which reminded us that giant, murderous space insects are in fact less awful than tech trillionaires. Continue reading...

data.title: An $18bn settlement – and Zuckerberg barely blinked. The tech titans must be stripped of their power, and soon | Jonathan Freedland
data.description: Those who said Meta harms children struck a blow, but the ability of big tech to gouge profits and cause harm is barely diminished. That’s the battle to come Follow the money. If you want to know how the tech giant Meta really feels about the $18bn it agreed to fork out to end a landmark lawsuit against it – an outcome widely hailed as a victory for campaigners – just look at its share price . It didn’t go down when word came on Wednesday that Meta had settled with the 29 US states that had argued that the company’s Facebook and Instagram platforms harmed children. On the contrary, Meta stock went up, initially surging by 5%, before levelling out at a gain of just over 1.25%. There could be no clearer proof that the money men reckon Meta dodged a bullet. To be sure, there was plenty to hearten those who have long believed that social media damages teenagers especially, whether by exposing them to content they shouldn’t see or by sapping their self-esteem, offering them filters that show how much prettier they would look if they had cosmetic surgery or giving them a metric of their popularity – and unpopularity – in the form of a running tally of “likes” and views. Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Nepal-Tibet flood: this is the cost of not acting in the face of the climate crisis | Sunil Acharya
data.description: Nepalis and Tibetans must not pay the price – with their lives, livelihoods and money meant for education and health – for global heating caused by wealthy states Sunil Acharya is an international climate policy and just transition specialist based in Kathmandu, Nepal As a Nepali citizen working on international climate policy for more than a decade, it is difficult to look at the harrowing images coming out of the catastrophic flash flood that thundered down valleys in Nepal, sweeping down the Lhende Khola, Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, and not feel angry. Not just because of the destruction, but because it comes after years of warnings from scientists and civil society that a rapidly warming planet would make disasters more frequent, more intense and harder to predict. This is what the cost of delaying global climate action looks like. data.title: Trump’s midterm campaign theme is unrequited love | Sidney Blumenthal
data.description: The president senses a crisis in his cult of personality. He believes the path to victory is through unwavering devotion Donald Trump has framed his theme for the midterm elections. It has come to him as naturally and inevitably as staring into the mirror, beyond any logic or argument, his definitive answer to no specific issue, providing no understanding of any particular problem, but transcending all of them. His political theme is more primal than programmatic, more instinctive than analytical, a heartfelt expression to protect his greatest romantic attachment, his obsessive fixation, his idealized object: himself. Trump’s campaign theme is unrequited love. Unlike the pollsters, media consultants and pundits, he alone has grasped the magnitude and the source of the existential crisis threatening his politics. He has identified the problem for the Republicans as the faltering measure of complete devotion to him. His demand has nothing to do with mutual affection. data.title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: prepare for more climate-linked disasters | Editorial
data.description: Medicine, food and other supplies are the urgent priority. But the rising risks from shrinking glaciers must be faced too Thousands of people in Nepal and Tibet are in desperate need of emergency assistance following Wednesday’s disaster. With 360 people confirmed dead, more than 1,300 others are still missing as search and rescue operations continue. The precise sequence of events linking glacier collapse to flash floods is yet to be confirmed. But there is no doubting the enormous destructive power of the brown torrent that can be seen on video clips surging down the steeply sided Himalayan valleys, sweeping away everyone and everything in its path. Testimony from survivors about terrifying near-escapes and losses is reminiscent of previous disasters, including the 2004 tsunami. With some of the worst-affected areas still cut off and accessible only by helicopter, there is a high level of uncertainty about the total number of people who have died or homes that have been destroyed. Existing medical, food, shelter and sanitation supplies will need to be replenished. Pledges of help for locally led relief efforts from foreign governments and agencies, following reports that hundreds of those missing were tourists or pilgrims, must lead to swift action. People need basics including electricity and clean water before they can start to rebuild and recover. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz to face Safiullin on return as Sabalenka gets tricky draw
data.description: Alcaraz back in action after four-month injury layoff Novak Djokovic faces Mariano Navone in first round Carlos Alcaraz has been handed a tough draw on his return to singles competition after a four-month injury layoff as he faces the in-form Russian Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open. Alcaraz, the defending champion in New York, has not competed in singles since sustaining a right wrist injury at the Barcelona Open in April, with the Spaniard missing the French Open, where he was also the defending champion, and Wimbledon. He was understandably rusty and tentative with his first serve when making his first competitive appearance since the injury alongside Serena Williams in the mixed doubles event on Tuesday, with the pair losing in the quarter-finals and the 44-year-old Williams even outperforming him during large parts of their time on court. His opening match against the world No 98 Safiullin, who has risen more than 100 places in the world rankings this year after returning from injury and defeated Alcaraz indoors at the Paris Masters in 2023, will be a significant first challenge. data.title: Aston Villa’s squad is crumbling while Spurs splash out. Are the financial rules fair?
data.description: Winning the Europa League and finishing fourth did not inoculate Villa and Spurs were not hampered by a season of woe In theory Aston Villa supporters should have been rubbing their hands together at the prospect of a Champions League season. Equally, Tottenham fans could have been despondent after a relegation battle that went to the wire. A 17th-place finish meant Spurs earned about £35m less in Premier League merit payments, which are based on final league position, than Villa. Yet the mood in the two camps is reversed. Spurs have spent an estimated £322m in the transfer window, and that excludes the loan of Manchester City’s Omar Marmoush, for whom they are committed to paying £55m after this season. Sales have reduced the outlay to a net £140m, but Spurs fans seemed buoyant, at least until the first match, when they were soundly thrashed by one of the data scientists’ teacher’s pets, Brentford. data.title: Esther González, Saudi Arabia and the questions around an unexpected transfer saga
data.description: The Gotham striker said she was stepping away from the sport, but then signed for Al Qadsiah. The move sparked questions over professionalism and raised concerns of LGBTQ+ fans who have disavowed the Saudi league A recent World Cup winner joins a historically downtrodden club, immediately leads them to their first championship, praises the level of play in the league, speaks fondly of living in the club’s market, extends her contract with the club, leads the club to another championship, is named a league MVP finalist, and breaks the club’s all-time scoring record. That’s the fairytale of Esther González and Gotham FC – a story that ended abruptly, just nine days after that scoring record was set. On 27 July, Gotham announced that they had mutually parted ways with the striker as she “temporarily steps away from soccer to attend to personal matters in Spain”. The announcement of her departure was full of gushing words going both directions, and was met with understanding and support from the women’s soccer world. But less than a month after González left Gotham, Al Qadsiah, a club in the Saudi Women’s Premier League, announced her as their newest signing, on a one-season contract with an option to extend for a second. NWSL journalist Jenna Tonelli soon reported , “League sources tell me that Gotham did not expect Esther to sign with another club this soon.” Questions swirled: did she actually intend to take a break from soccer when she left Gotham? And why would a player who just had a child with her female partner choose to play in Saudi Arabia, a country where same-sex relations are criminalized? Continue reading...

data.title: Managerial turnover means we need new ways to predict Premier League fixtures
data.description: With 110 matches to feature two coaches appointed this year, tactical history may be more insightful than teams’ head-to-head records New managers are facing an almost one-in-two chance of being fired before the end of the season, a finding from Guardian analysis that shows 22 of the past 50 permanent Premier League managers to leave their roles lasted less than a year. The betting markets reflect this reality. Six of the eight Premier League managers deemed most likely by bookmakers to be next to leave their post were appointed in 2026. Football management is a very precarious employment position. It looks inevitable that some of the 11 men who have only been in their role since earlier this year will fall before the end of the 2026-27 season – even if none of them are the first to move on. Continue reading...

data.title: Air pollution affects us all, but there is a way we can breathe easier
data.description: In this week’s newsletter: pollutants from fossil fuels and wildfires damage nearly every part of our bodies – but initiatives such as cycle zones can make our cities safer • Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Air pollution affects nearly every person on this planet . Yet global efforts to combat the scourge – which is associated with about 8 million premature deaths worldwide every year, can damage nearly every part of our body and is linked to everything from miscarriages to dementia – lag decades behind our knowledge of its impacts. Tens of millions of people in Indonesia are now suffering in swathes of thick smoke caused by “slash and burn” agriculture and exacerbated by the hot conditions. In India, ground-level ozone from vehicle fumes and industry has emerged as the key summer threat, while outside its megacities there have been protests in areas affected by toxic coal dust. Across the northern hemisphere this summer, wildfires driven by the climate crisis have spread poor air across continents – already, 1.5 million people globally die every year from the impacts of wildfire smoke. data.title: ‘It’s the story of what happens when the music stops’: bringing tormented jazz legend Bill Evans to life
data.description: Having directed documentaries about David Bowie, Radiohead and Joy Division, Grant Gee takes on a biopic of the turbulent and tragic American pianist In 1997, Grant Gee directed the video for Radiohead’s single No Surprises , a four-minute film that featured Thom Yorke miming the song inside a water-filled diver’s helmet, apparently almost drowning in the process. In the three decades since that promo, Gee has made a host of diverse feature-length films about artists: Radiohead, David Bowie, Joy Division, the Turkish Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk , the émigré German novelist WG Sebald . They are often impressionistic, dreamlike explorations of art, memory, place and the strange pressures put upon artistic lives. “It’s a narrative form I’ve used again and again,” says Gee. “A character begins in one condition; a crisis slowly develops; the viewer watches that crisis in a forensic yet empathetic way; the crisis passes; the person returns to something like the original state, but transformed. Someone comes very close to drowning, but doesn’t drown. What does that do to them?” Continue reading...

data.title: The Secret Woman review – Claes Bang is dastardly gaslighter in Danish amnesia thriller
data.description: In spite of capable performances and deployment of hygge , gothic and Nordic noir elements, you’ll search for a feasible plot or a character insight in vain Adapted from the 2017 novel by Anna Ekberg (actually a male writing duo), this thriller from Denmark chucks in a bit of everything into the mix: hygge lakeside melodrama, manor-house gothic, and Nordic-noir corruption. But this franticness can’t disguise that it’s a dopey and facile thriller that, despite capable performances, plumbs neither its characters’ depths nor hits thematic pay dirt. It also merits a stiff investigation from the plotting police. Despite amnesia that leaves her unable to remember her life prior to running an idyllic Norwegian rural cafe, Louise (Natalie Wolfsberg Madueño) is gearing up to get hitched to crime writer Joachim (Pål Sverre Hagen). When a tourist approaches and calls her by another name, she is sufficiently shaken to take a DNA test; it confirms she is actually Helene Söderberg, a Danish shipping heiress presumed dead, with a husband and son back home. Originally found stowed away on a cargo ship, she handed over an ID card – for Louise Anderson – which the authorities accepted. Now wanting to reclaim her identity, she pitches up on the capacious doorstep of company executive Edmund (Claes Bang), her former partner. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m not even an actor – I was just grieving!’ Rising star Lara Ricote on the heartache behind her new breakup comedy
data.description: The Mexican-American comedian had just split from her boyfriend when she filmed Break Clause, about an ex-couple living together in London. She talks trading telenovelas for Edinburgh and embracing your feelings • The 50 best TV shows of autumn 2026 In Break Clause, recent graduates Lil and Ben move from Leeds to London after the former lands a job at an architecture firm. Yet as soon as the couple start settling into their new flat, everything goes horribly wrong. Ben ( Samuel Bottomley ) reveals he slept with someone else at their leaving drinks the night before, so Lil (Lara Ricote) immediately ends the relationship – but quickly discovers their rental contract is far harder to get out of. Cue an agonising six months of cohabitation and a novel will-they-won’t-they (get back together) setup for a winningly bittersweet new sitcom. You may recognise Ricote from recent appearances in two other Channel 4 comedies: Mitchell and Webb Are Not Helping and Sam Campbell’s crackers Make That Movie (although probably not from the “funny and crazy” telenovela she briefly worked on as a teen). But Break Clause is the Mexican-American comedian’s first leading role. It also happened to be the “best case scenario” for Ricote’s debut: let’s just say getting into character wasn’t a problem. data.title: The Whisper Man review – Robert De Niro sleepwalks through silly Netflix potboiler
data.description: A father and son must team up to find a serial killer in a cheaply made and increasingly uninteresting thriller It’s not as if Robert De Niro ’s choices have improved all that much since the nadir of the mid-2000s (last year did see him crop up in a Scott Eastwood-led actioner and The Alto Knights ) but there’s something specifically rubbishy about his latest that transports us back to that particularly cursed time. The Whisper Man, a film as openly stupid as its title would suggest, could have been released in between the evil clone horror Godsend and imaginary friend thriller Hide and Seek , the kind of bottom-tier project that offers the actor a nice big cheque and the audience a nice little nap. It’s a familiar pile of B-movie schlock – serial killers, missing children, bumps in the night, more imaginary friends – and there is some initial junky fun to be had as we wonder just where it all might be headed. I was hoping for a destination a little more deranged or vaguely surprising, the film making a silent promise that we’re hurtling toward somewhere wildly unexpected before dumping us in a ditch instead. Continue reading...

data.title: Klara Lewis: Opening review – enigmatic, ecstatic sound sculptures from a Swedish slowburn master
data.description: (Editions Mego) Lewis mines beauty and intimacy from her minimalist blend of samples and rich instrumentation, sounding as profound whether they last 11 minutes or 38 seconds The first thing you hear on Opening, the new record from Swedish musician Klara Lewis, is a grainy fog of ambient noise: the sound of waves, a roadside or perhaps just the creaks and echoes of the room she’s recording in. The whining reversed strings that soon emerge from the murk create a wistful atmosphere, but then things take a turn: the loop clips and distorts with strobe-like intensity; after several minutes, it cuts off mid-bar, as though it’s been unplugged. This deconstructed, shape-shifting approach is typical of the self-styled “sound sculptor”, who has been composing uncanny instrumentals from a combination of acoustic instruments and processed samples since 2014. As always, she imbues the harsh experimentalism with real feeling throughout this gorgeous collection of tracks. On City, the lo-fi guitar loop and faint traces of chatter lend a sense of warmth and intimacy to the whooshing field recordings and churning electronics. On standout Vaknar, Lewis builds something soaring and beautiful, where the reverse tape effect creates a dreamlike wooziness and the high-pitched bursts of noise feel increasingly ecstatic, in the spirit of Joshua Chuquimia Crampton or early Arca. Continue reading...

data.title: Dahi: Black Boy (Alternative) review – Kendrick producer takes the spotlight for all-star guitar celebration
data.description: (ALTER) The Grammy winner unites former clients including Lamar and Ravyn Lenae for a playful, dazzling voyage through the guitar’s diversity, from alt-rock to Afrobeat On this long-awaited debut, Grammy-winning hip-hop producer Dahi steps out from the booth and into the spotlight. He’s best known for transforming a dreamy Beach House sample into Kendrick Lamar’s hit Money Trees, alongside chameleonic production work for SZA, Madonna, Drake and many more. Now that Dahi’s got the mic, what does he want to say? Blending the brittle 90s British rock he loved as a California teen with the west African grooves his father played in the house, Black Boy (Alternative) celebrates the guitar as a transcendent tool that spans genres and continents. No other album this year will boast such starry guest features – Dahi calls up former clients Lamar, Childish Gambino, Vince Staples and Ravyn Lenae alongside experimentalists such as Moses Sumney, Baby Rose and Fousheé – but it’s testament to the strength of his vision that these distinct voices come together like a bedded-in, playful house band. All trust, no ego. Continue reading...

data.title: Donnacha Dennehy: Limina album review – joyously unfettered music is a thrill in motion
data.description: McCarthy/Waarts/National Symphony Orchestra Ireland/McAdams (Nonesuch) Dennehy’s Limina, based on areas of the body, is firmly grounded in the harmonic series, and sparklingly executed here, while Stephen Waarts gives a bravura performance of the Violin Concerto These two concertos, beautifully paired, again find Donnacha Dennehy writing music that is both firmly grounded – both rhythmically and in his fascination with the harmonic series – and, to the ear at least, joyously unfettered. Limina was written in 2023 for the pianist Eliza McCarthy , who is a powerhouse soloist here with the National Symphony Orchestra Ireland and conductor Ryan McAdams . It’s a serious piece born of a slightly playful idea. Its three movements are each named for a part of the body, staking out one area before moving to the threshold, or limina, of the next. Head starts with synapses firing high up the keyboard in sparks and glitter; it travels downwards, frenetic energy dissipating, towards Chest, which evokes breathing – not with regular rhythms but with gentle palindromic phrases that swell in and out and sigh back towards the same bass pitch. Nervous System begins deep in the gut, with coarser sounds – low piano vamping, and slapped bowing from the strings – but eventually escapes its tether and disperses around the keyboard. The Violin Concerto, written in 2020, is just as propulsive, and the outer movements especially are a workout for Stephen Waarts , who gives a bravura performance. In the middle movement his violin soars, pushing off from the orchestral support to trace slow, weightless somersaults in the air. The finale has a thrilling sense of motion creating its own gravity: as with so much of Dennehy’s writing, it’s as if the music is held together by centrifugal force. Continue reading...

data.title: Sophie, Standing There by Meg Mason review – a tale of literary obsession, with cameos from real-life authors
data.description: A heartbroken woman becomes fixated on a famous writer in this witty, touching follow-up to Sorrow and Bliss The protagonist of Meg Mason’s new book, the follow-up to the 2020 tragicomedy Sorrow and Bliss , is an invisible woman. She might well be standing there but you won’t notice her. She’s a techie at literary festivals – the person who shuffles up to a famous writer a few minutes before their event and apologetically slides a microphone cable down their shirt while they’re making small talk with the chair or accepting a bottle of room-temperature mineral water from an anxious publicist. No man is a hero to his valet, and no writer is a hero to the technical staff lurking in the wings of a venue. Mason’s opening pages present a teasing but not quite libellous series of cameos from real writers: George Saunders deciding at an inconsiderately late stage to insist on swapping his headset for a lapel mic; Ann Patchett being frosty with a fan; Mick Herron accidentally stepping on someone’s foot and not apologising. Continue reading...

data.title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past – Geralt of Rivia returns after a decade in the sun
data.description: Before The Witcher 4 arrives in 2028, CD Projekt Red is returning us to the world of The Witcher 3 for one last foray. Looks like wind’s still howlin’ The game that graced us with Bathtub Geralt , The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, arrived more than a decade ago. So it was a touch surprising this summer when developers CD Projekt Red announced a new expansion to the venerable adventure, titled Songs of the Past, for next year. It will release alongside a full remaster of the original game, which will be free for anyone who bought it back in 2015. (The studio is also working on a sequel, The Witcher 4, but that’s not due until 2028.) As it turns out, this is all possible thanks to a partnership with Fool’s Theory, a studio founded by CD Projekt Red veterans, which took on the brunt of the development work. “We’ve had this story in a drawer for many years,” explains Marcin Blacha, VP story director at CD Projekt Red. “Of course, we moved on to Cyberpunk 2077 and now The Witcher 4, as well as our other projects. But because we knew The Witcher 4 would take time, we saw a gap in our release calendar where Songs of the Past could go. It will release alongside a full remaster of the original game, which will be free for anyone who bought it back in 2015. data.title: Help! I have disappeared down a rabbithole of horrible mobile gaming adverts | Dominik Diamond
data.description: Led by the nose from game to terrible game by increasingly disturbing and terrible adverts, I feel like I’m in the cinema scene from A Clockwork Orange We’re all escaping something when we play video games. Mostly it’s the drabness of real life, where we don’t get to command kingdoms using armies of dragons, win Champions League trophies with our local team, or inhabit the body of an improbably speedy hedgehog. Sometimes I play them because I want to escape from the version of me that gets paralysed by depression, and boy has the black dog been sniffing at my bits recently, because the Atlantic Ocean is separating me from my wife for a few months. For 30 years she has been the light that banishes that darkness, and I am honestly lost without her. If that sounds pathetic, you haven’t met her. She leaves everybody she meets feeling better. It’s a superpower that warrants a call from the X-Men. Continue reading...

data.title: Experience: I brought a bear back to life
data.description: I was in India, performing dentistry on my first animal patient, and it was supposed to be a straightforward operation I’ve been a dentist for 40 years. I spend most of my time treating patients at my surgery in Chichester, West Sussex. When I studied to become a dentist in the 1980s, I didn’t think I’d be getting my hands anywhere near the teeth of any exotic animals. Twenty years later, in 2000, that changed. A patient of mine, Alan Knight, the CEO of International Animal Rescue (IAR), showed me photographs of the inside of a bear’s mouth. The bear was called Jojo and his teeth had been broken off by poachers. Some of the teeth were too rotten to be saved – if left untreated, Jojo would become more prone to infection and abscesses. Continue reading...

data.title: Relocated turtle nests produced fewer hatchlings, smaller young and a heavily female-biased sex ratio
data.description: Relocating vulnerable sea turtle nests can lead to unexpected negative consequences. When nests are moved to warmer areas, the sex ratio of hatchlings skews heavily towards females. Additionally, even nests placed in shaded locations yield smaller hatchlings with reduced physical capabilities. Therefore, effective nest relocation must consider various environmental factors beyond just temperature to ensure the successful recovery of turtle populations.

data.title: German tourist returns stolen skull to Vienna cathedral after 60 years with a final confession
data.description: A human skull that was stolen from the catacombs of St. Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna has been returned to its rightful place. The elderly German tourist who had taken it as a young man confessed after sixty long years, seeking closure for his past actions. Although the identity of the original owner is a mystery, this return marks the resolution of a tale filled with youthful folly and subsequent regret.

data.title: Nepal floods: How recent reports warned of this disaster months ago
data.description: Recent floods in Nepal and Tibet followed ICIMOD's warnings about melting glaciers.  These reports highlighted doubled ice loss rates and increased flood risks across the region.  A catastrophic flash flood triggered by a glacier collapse killed hundreds and left many missing.  Smaller glaciers are shrinking faster, intensifying hazards like glacial lake outburst floods.  Regional cooperation is vital for understanding and preparing for these cross-border mountain disasters.

data.title: Scientists turn wood waste into foam that replaces plastic and decomposes in soil within months
data.description: Canada is piloting a new process to convert wood waste into biodegradable foam. This innovative material is designed to replace plastic foam packaging and construction insulation. The pilot plant in Vancouver currently produces a limited amount of this eco-friendly wood foam. Future plans include expanding production significantly within Indigenous territories and on Vancouver Island. This initiative aims to create jobs and foster economic opportunities for Indigenous communities.

data.description:

On Monday, Iran and Oman agreed in principle to a temporary maritime route for ships travelling through the Strait of Hormuz. This could lead to the easing of the tit-for-tat blockades imposed by Iran and the US if President Donald Trump’s administration accepts it.

data.title: D. Yolanda só queria um dia livre para compras
data.description: Há alguns anos, fui contratada para fazer uma pesquisa em arquivos diplomáticos dos anos 1960. No meio de milhares de memorandos sobre as relações entre o Brasil e os Estados Unidos , encontrei comentários inusitados de oficiais americanos sobre seus pares brasileiros: "Está ficando careca", "Tem um carro muito velho", "Conta piadas de mau gosto", "Gosta de ver novela com a mulher". Passei a fazer duas pesquisas: a encomendada e uma outra sobre fofocas velhas da diplomacia. Numa época pré-internet, quando não era fácil obter fotografias, as descrições físicas tinham destaque nos relatórios. Leia mais (08/28/2026 - 10h00)

data.title: Fei-Fei Li: de ‘peetmoeder van AI’ die computers leerde kijken en nu bouwt aan de volgende fase
data.description: AI-pionier Fei-Fei Li maakte furore met ImageNet; ze leerde computers ‘kijken’. Na een conflict bij Google rondom de inzet van AI voor defensietoepassingen, richtte ze World Labs op. AI moet de mensheid dienen, vindt Li, die zich profileert als de nuchtere stem tussen techleiders die utopieën of juist nachtmerries verkopen. Maar ook zij is afhankelijk van financiers die rendement zoeken.

data.title: Posłuchaj „Plus Minus”: Tomasz Kołodziejczak o 250 latach polskiej fantastyki naukowej
data.description: Czy polska fantastyka naukowa rzeczywiście ma własny, rozpoznawalny styl? Dlaczego rodzimi autorzy tak chętnie wykorzystywali przyszłość, inne planety i wymyślone społeczeństwa, by opowiadać o problemach własnej epoki? I czy gatunek, który przez dekady próbował wyobrażać sobie przyszłość, jest dziś gotowy na największą zmianę – pojawienie się sztucznej inteligencji zdolnej samodzielnie tworzyć historie? O tych paradoksach, sukcesach i ograniczeniach polskiego science fiction Daria Chibner rozmawia z Tomaszem Kołodziejczakiem w podcaście „Posłuchaj Plus Minus”.

data.title: Islanďané jsou rozpolcení nad obnovením jednání s EU, vyplývá z nového průzkumu
data.description: Těsná většina islandských voličů by nepodpořila obnovení jednání o členství země v Evropské unii, vyplynulo z nového průzkumu. Jde o rozdílný výsledek oproti předchozím průzkumům, které proběhly před sobotním referendem, poznamenala agentura Reuters. Islanďané nebudou hlasovat o samotném členství v nynější sedmadvacítce, ale pouze o tom, zda mají opět začít přístupové rozhovory.

data.title: Čtvrtina Čechů nechodí na preventivní prohlídky. Vojtěch chce motivovat penězi
data.description: Účast Čechů na preventivních prohlídkách se každoročně zlepšuje, nicméně čtvrtina dospělých nechodí na žádné, vyplývá z průzkumu Stada Health Report 2026. O možnosti motivace lidí k prevenci se zajímá i ministerstvo zdravotnictví. Ministr Adam Vojtěch prosazuje, aby pojišťovny finančně odměňovaly ty, kteří na prevence chodí. Ti, kteří se o své zdraví starají, by se tak mohli dočkat bonusu v řádu tisíců.

data.title: Přes půl světa za jediným hráčem. Jak si Japonci zamilovali baseball v Brně
data.description: Let přes půl světa, nejméně 50 tisíc korun za cestu a několik dní v Brně. To vše kvůli baseballovému zápasu. Do hlediště brněnských Draků letos míří fanoušci až z Japonska. data.title: Mimořádná osobnost, napsali Pavel a Babiš o zesnulém norském králi
data.description: Norský král Harald V. zanechává výraznou stopu nejen v moderních dějinách Norska, ale také v evropském a mezinárodním veřejném životě. V kondolenčním telegramu to v pátek uvedl prezident Petr Pavel. Vyjádřil v něm upřímnou soustrast novému králi Haakonovi VIII., celé královské rodině a občanům Norska. Soustrast vyjádřili i další politici.

data.title: Strom může vypadat zdravě, i když umírá. Satelity to poznají dřív než člověk
data.description: Brněnská firma ASITIS s projektem UpGreen pomocí satelitních snímků sleduje kondici městských stromů. Dokáže porovnávat jejich stav několik let zpětně a upozornit na ty, které začínají mít problém. Podle odborníků přitom nestačí stromy ve městech pouze vysazovat. Klíčové je dostat je do věku, kdy začnou skutečně poskytovat ekosystémové služby.

data.title: Náhoda? Nemyslím si! Věštec jaderné zkázy zmizel z ruské televize
data.description: „Rusko je jediná země, která má kapacity obrátit Spojené státy v jaderný popel,“ prohlásil kdysi Dmitrij Kiseljov. data.title: Podpora v nezaměstnanosti se změní. Ministerstvo plánuje ušetřit 4,5 miliardy
data.description: Ministerstvo práce plánuje návrat k předchozímu nastavení podpor v nezaměstnanosti a snížení částek od ledna. Příští rok tak chce ušetřit asi 4,5 miliardy korun na výdajích. Částka by v prvních měsících znovu klesla z 80 procent výdělku na 65 procent. Maximální podpora by činila 60 procent průměrné mzdy místo letošních 80 procent, sdělil odbor komunikace ministerstva práce. Proti se staví odbory, zaměstnavatelé i odborníci.

data.title: Změna termínů prázdnin? Plaga to odmítá, opozice nebyla proti
data.description: Začátkem srpna vyvolal ministr školství Robert Plaga bouři, když se lidí zeptal, jestli jim termín letních prázdnin vyhovuje, nebo chtějí změnu. Žáci, rodiče i učitelé Plagu okamžitě zavalili návrhy a postupně se oživily i staré smělé plány na úpravu školního roku. Na „prázdninové evoluci“ chtěla s Plagou začít spolupracovat i část opozice. Jenže ministr sám se do práce na změnách pouštět nechce.

data.title: Bird flu kills 13,000 seal pups on remote Australian island
data.description:
SYDNEY: A pathogenic strain of bird flu killed more than 13,000 elephant seal pups after infecting a breeding colony on a sub-Antarctic volcanic island, Australian scientists said Thursday.
	Researchers found the remote Heard and McDonald Islands littered with seal carcasses when they arrived on a research expedition in October 2025.
	Genetic testing confirmed the contagious H5 bird flu strain had killed seals, penguins and birds living on the rocky outcrop — the first time it had been detected in one of Australia’s external territories.

data.title: Australia says net migration down as far-right popularity surges
data.description:
SYDNEY: Australia’s immigration levels fell last year, official data showed on Thursday, as its center-left government seeks to combat an ascendent far-right riding a wave of public discontent over soaring housing prices and cost of living.
	Net overseas migration added 301,000 people to Australia’s population of 28 million last year, Canberra’s Bureau of Statistics reported.
	Immigration minister Tony Burke said the figure was down nine percent from a year earlier and 45 percent lower than a post-Covid peak in 2023.

data.title: Kane double fires England World Cup bid as Ronaldo’s Portugal stumble
data.description:

data.title: Oil falls to 3-1/2-month low after US, Iran sign ceasefire deal
data.description:
BEIJING/SINGAPORE: Oil prices ​fell by more than $2 per barrel on Thursday after the US and Iran signed an interim agreement that ‌would end the Iran war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz and waive US sanctions on Tehran’s oil, boosting the oil supply outlook.

	Brent crude futures were down $2.14, or 2.69 percent, at $77.41 a barrel as of 09:16 a.m. Saudi time, and US West Texas Intermediate fell $2.36, or 3.07 percent, to $74.43 a barrel.

data.title: Daily Telegraph columnist argues Saudi Arabia should join G7
data.description:
DUBAI: Saudi Arabia should be invited to join the Group of Seven nations as the organization adapts to a changing global order, according to a column published in the Daily Telegraph by former UK prime ministerial representative to Saudi Arabia Ken Costa.

	Costa argued that while the G7 was created in the aftermath of the 1970s oil crisis, the world has changed dramatically since then, with new economic and geopolitical powers emerging. Despite those shifts, he said the group remains largely unchanged and no longer reflects the realities of global influence.

data.title: Tacna: 97 años de una reincorporación marcada por la resistencia y amor al Perú [INFORME]
data.description: A 97 años de su reincorporación al Perú, Tacna mantiene viva una historia de resistencia que atravesó casi medio siglo de ocupación chilena. La lucha por preservar la identidad peruana, el papel de las mujeres tacneñas y la tradicional Procesión de la Bandera mantienen vigente una memoria que se transmite de generación en generación.

data.title: Sismo de magnitud 3,6 en Mérida provocó evacuación de edificios, centros comerciales e instituciones públicas
data.description: El movimiento telúrico ocurrió a las 11:36 am y tuvo profundidad de 5,0 kilómetros. Funvisis había reportado antes otros tres sismos. data.title: Palau Earth Day Committee Celebrates World Mangrove Day with Clean-Up at Ngemai Conservation Area

data.title: Crise anglophone : un tribunal fédéral américain condamne trois Américains d’origine camerounaise
data.description: © DR Jugés coupables d'avoir fourni du soutien financier et logistique pour la fabrication et l'utilisation des engins explosifs improvisés au Cameroun, ils n'échappent pas à de lourdes peines. Ils écopent des peines allant de cinq à 15 ans de prison ferme. Francis Chenyi âgé de 52 ans, Lah Nestor Langmi, 49 ans tombent sous le coup d'une condamnation de 15 ans de prison chacun. Tandis que Claude Ngenevu Chi, 43 ans, doit purger 63 mois de prison correspondant à un peu plus de 5 ans. Après avoir purgé les différentes peines, les trois condamnés seront soumis chacun à trois ans de liberté surveillée. Ainsi a décidé le tribunal fédéral de Kansas City dans le Missouri. Il est reproché aux trois ressortissants camerounais d'avoir appartenu à un réseau de financement et de fourniture de la logistique au profit des combattants séparatistes qui opèrent dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest. Ils ont exercé des missions de coordination des opérations de fabrication des engins explosifs improvisés ainsi que de la formation des personnes en vue de leur utilisation, apprend-on de sources médiatiques. Des mêmes sources, cette coordination s'étend aussi à des attaques à l'aide de ces explosifs en ciblant plusieurs villes du Nord-Ouest et à proximité du stade devant accueillir la CAN 2021 dans la région du Sud-Ouest. Aussi, la justice reproche à ces trois hommes d'avoir coordonné des opérations de transfert des fonds des États-Unis vers le Cameroun. Des fonds qui ont servi à réaliser des projets d'attaques évoqués plus haut. De manière individuelle, la justice reproche à Langmi d'avoir participé à la coordination des opérations d'enlèvements dont celui du chef traditionnel Fonmbam Aforteka et celui du cardinal Christian Tumi de regrettée mémoire. Pour la commission de ces faits, Chenyi aurait fourni une contribution financière. Ce sont ainsi trois financiers de plus de la crise anglophone qui sont condamnés par la justice américaine dans le cadre du règlement de la crise. Depuis quelques années, d'autres Camerounais ont écopé des condamnations à des peines diverses presque pour les mêmes motifs. Che Ernest Banhary et Edith Ngang ont écopé de quatre ans de prison ferme. En 2024, une trentaine de leaders séparatistes ont été traduits devant les juridictions américaines à la suite de plusieurs plaintes déposées par le cabinet Me Nsahlai à la demande de l'Etat camerounais. Les États-Unis se sont engagés à poursuivre juger et condamner ces hommes suspectés d'avoir participé à financer ou à commettre des actes terroristes sur le territoire camerounais. Cet article Crise anglophone : un tribunal fédéral américain condamne trois Américains d’origine camerounaise est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

En 2024, une trentaine de leaders séparatistes ont été traduits devant les juridictions américaines à la suite de plusieurs plaintes déposées par le cabinet Me Nsahlai à la demande de l'Etat camerounais. Les États-Unis se sont engagés à poursuivre juger et condamner ces hommes suspectés d'avoir participé à financer ou à commettre des actes terroristes sur le territoire camerounais. data.title: Coopération Cameroun-UNFPA : le 9e Programme Pays validé à 50 millions USD
data.description: © DR 50 millions de dollars, 3 piliers stratégiques, un partenariat depuis 1969. Le Conseil d'Administration de l'UNFPA a approuvé le 27 août 2026 à New York le 9e Programme de Coopération avec le Cameroun (2027-2031), aligné sur la SND30 et l'UNSDCF. C’est le quitus officiel. Le Conseil d’Administration de l’UNFPA a validé le 27 août 2026 le nouveau Programme de Coopération Pays (CPD9) axé sur le bien-être des populations et le dividende démographique. Fruit d’une concertation menée par le MINEPAT et le MINREX en alignement avec le cadre UNSDCF 2027-2031 et la Stratégie Nationale de Développement SND30, le programme pérennise un partenariat historique initié en 1969. Présentant l’aval du gouvernement à New York, la Mission Permanente du Cameroun a déclaré : "Ma délégation note avec satisfaction l'alignement du document sur la SND30 et le cadre UNSDCF. Le Gouvernement exprime son ferme soutien au 9e Programme Pays et invite le Conseil à l'approuver." Doté d’un budget indicatif de 50 millions USD, le CPD9 vise trois piliers d’ici 2031 : qualité des soins et santé reproductive avec accès universel à la planification familiale et réduction des décès maternels, égalité de genre et autonomisation avec éradication des violences basées sur le genre, et données démographiques pour des politiques publiques informées. Pour accompagner l’expansion, Yaoundé offre un nouveau siège moderne à l’UNFPA, s’affirmant comme partenaire clé grâce à la mobilisation conjointe du MINEPAT, MINREX, MINSANTE, MINPROFF, MINJEC et MINFI. Cet article Coopération Cameroun-UNFPA : le 9e Programme Pays validé à 50 millions USD est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Violences sur le genre au Cameroun : les techniques de riposte proposées par la LEFE
data.description: © DR La Ligue pour l’éducation de la femme et de l'enfant (Lefe) dénonce la recrudescence des féminicides, indique les signaux d’alarme et exige l'adoption des lois pour résoudre le phénomène. La situation est alarmante. Huit femmes tuées en l'espace de huit jours, plus 60 au cours de l'année 2026. 1 599 cas de violences basées sur le genre dont 166 viols relevés entre janvier et avril 2026. La Lefe qualifie la situation de crime nationale dans un plaidoyer récent. L'organisation non gouvernementale réactive sa position de défense en faveur des femmes et rouvre des pistes menant à des solutions tant préventives que dépressives. Face à la situation qui s'aggrave et contre laquelle un vent d'indignation souffle de manière intermittente, l'organisation indique à titre préventif quelques signaux qui alertent sur l'imminence des violences. Des menaces de mort, des menaces d'enlèvement d'enfants, l'étranglement même dans marque, la disponibilité de l'arme, l'intensification des violences, des coups pendant la grossesse, des rapports sexuels imposés, la traque ou la filature, la séparation récente indiquent un danger élevé ou immédiat. Ce cas de figure mérite des mesures immédiates de la part de la victime. D'autres signes comme l'isolement de la famille et des amis, le contrôle du téléphone et de l'argent, les humiliations, la jalousie extrême ou l'interdiction de travailler sont à prendre à considération avant que l'auteur aille plus loin. A celles qui sont devant ces comportements qui activent l'alerte, la Lefe recommande de se mettre à l'abri, d'éviter de confronter l'adversaire seul, de faire constater les violences pour conserver les preuves. Au-delà de ces mesures individuelles à prendre en cas de signaux, la lutte contre les violences est une affaire collective. La Lefe propose aussi l'adoption d'une loi contre le féminicide et les violences faites aux femmes et aux enfants. Une législation prévoyant des mesures d'éloignement de la victime en 24 heures. À cette loi, l'organisation propose d'associer le code des personnes et de la famille dont l'adoption est attendue depuis 20 ans. Ledit code permettra de garantir l'égalité dans le mariage, les biens, la succession et la garde des enfants. Le chapelet de propositions fait aussi référence à la mobilisation d'un budget dédié pour faciliter l'application de ces textes. La batterie de mesures oriente des décideurs en les invitant à passer de la condamnation des actes de violence à l'action concrète. Cet article Violences sur le genre au Cameroun : les techniques de riposte proposées par la LEFE est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Désertification : la BAD réclame plus de financements pour les zones de conflit
data.description: © DR À Oulan-Bator, la 17e Conférence des Nations Unies sur la lutte contre la désertification a réuni 12 000 délégués autour du thème "Restaurer les terres". La BAD y a plaidé pour un financement accru des terres dégradées dans les régions fragiles d’Afrique. L’Afrique fragile au cœur du sommet des terres. Lors de la COP17 de la Convention sur la lutte contre la désertification tenue à Oulan-Bator en Mongolie, le Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement a lancé un appel fort : accroître les financements pour restaurer les terres dégradées dans les régions fragiles et touchées par les conflits. Intitulée "Redonner espoir" et placée sous le thème "Restaurer les terres", la conférence a réuni plus de 12 000 représentants des 197 États parties pour accélérer l’action mondiale contre la désertification, la dégradation des terres et la sécheresse. Une rencontre cruciale au moment où les États tentent de transformer les engagements internationaux en actions concrètes. Pour la BAD, restaurer les terres en Afrique n’est pas qu’une question environnementale : c’est un levier de sécurité alimentaire, de résilience climatique et de moyens de subsistance durables dans des zones où la dégradation nourrit l’instabilité. Le message est clair : sans financement ciblé pour les territoires fragiles, l’ambition de neutralité en matière de dégradation des terres restera lettre morte. Cet article Désertification : la BAD réclame plus de financements pour les zones de conflit est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Riposte aux épidémies : le Cameroun déploie sa première Équipe Médicale d’Urgence
data.description: © DR C’est une première historique. Du 24 au 28 août à Ebolowa, le Cameroun forme sa toute première Équipe Médicale d’Urgence (EMU), une unité multidisciplinaire de 80 experts prête à intervenir en cas d’épidémies et de catastrophes. Le Cameroun franchit un cap dans sa sécurité sanitaire. À Ebolowa, dans la région du Sud, 80 professionnels suivent depuis le 24 août la formation intensive de la toute première EMU nationale. Médecins, paramédicaux, mais aussi logisticiens, experts en communication, sécurité, soutien, santé mentale, santé reproductive et nutrition : l’équipe réunit 26 profils répartis en deux groupes. Une composition assumée : une épidémie ne se combat pas qu’en blouse blanche. Pendant cinq jours, 7 modules sont dispensés : gestion des urgences de santé publique, Prévention et Contrôle des Infections (PCI), promotion de la santé et engagement communautaire (CREC), sans oublier les ateliers pratiques d’habillage/déshabillage des EPI et les exercices de terrain pour apprendre à fonctionner comme une seule équipe. L’enjeu est politique : ne pas remplacer le système existant mais le renforcer. L’EMU est une capacité opérationnelle supplémentaire, mobilisable rapidement sans désorganiser les hôpitaux. Le projet, inspiré des modèles sénégalais et tchadien, bénéficie de l’appui technique de l’OMS et du soutien financier d’ECHO / Commission européenne. Le Cameroun se prépare pour mieux protéger. Cet article Riposte aux épidémies : le Cameroun déploie sa première Équipe Médicale d’Urgence est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Décentralisation : le Cameroun veut intégrer les réfugiés dans les budgets communaux
data.description: © DR "La prise en compte des réfugiés commence dans la commune." Le message a été martelé à Yaoundé le 27 août 2026 où le MINDDEVEL et le HCR ont présenté leur plan conjoint pour inclure les réfugiés dans les plans de développement local. L’inclusion locale au cœur de la politique des réfugiés. À Yaoundé, le Ministère de la Décentralisation et du Développement Local et le Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies pour les Réfugiés ont présenté leur plan de travail conjoint le 27 août 2026. L'objectif est de mieux intégrer les besoins des réfugiés dans les plans et budgets des Collectivités Territoriales Décentralisées. La rencontre a réuni maires, représentants du gouvernement, partenaires techniques et financiers, et réfugiés eux-mêmes. Les échanges ont souligné le rôle de première ligne des communes et régions dans la promotion de l’inclusion socio-économique et la recherche de solutions durables. Au-delà de l’accueil humanitaire, il s’agit de faire des CTD le levier du vivre-ensemble. Le gouvernement a appelé les partenaires à renforcer leur appui aux collectivités engagées pour un développement local inclusif, résilient et bénéfique à la fois aux réfugiés et aux communautés hôtes. Cet article Décentralisation : le Cameroun veut intégrer les réfugiés dans les budgets communaux est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Éducation : vers un cadre curriculaire unifié, le Cameroun harmonise ses outils de diagnostic
data.description: © DR Le Cameroun franchit une étape clé vers l’unification de son système éducatif. Un atelier technique réunit cette semaine MINEDUB, MINESEC, UNESCO et UNICEF pour valider les outils de collecte qui serviront à bâtir un cadre curriculaire commun. C’est une étape fondatrice pour l’école camerounaise. Un atelier consacré au développement et au renforcement des capacités en matière d’outils de collecte de données se tient cette semaine, en vue de l’élaboration d’un cadre curriculaire unifié. L’initiative s’inscrit dans le Programme d’Appui à la Professionnalisation du Métier de l’Enseignant au Cameroun (PAPMEC), soutenu par le Partenariat mondial pour l’éducation et mis en œuvre conjointement par le MINEDUB et le MINESEC, avec l’appui de l’UNESCO et de l’UNICEF. Avec l’appui technique du Bureau international d’éducation de l’UNESCO, la mission est décisive : développer, harmoniser et valider de manière participative les instruments de collecte - questionnaires, guides d’entretien, grilles d’observation qui permettront de recueillir des informations fiables sur les pratiques, les besoins et les attentes de tous les acteurs du système éducatif. Plus qu’une simple production technique, cet exercice pose les bases du futur Document cadre d’orientation curriculaire commun, qui devra fédérer cinq ministères : MINEDUB, MINESEC, MINESUP, MINJEC et MINEFOP. L’enjeu est politique : mettre fin à la fragmentation des programmes et professionnaliser durablement le métier d’enseignant au Cameroun. Cet article Éducation : vers un cadre curriculaire unifié, le Cameroun harmonise ses outils de diagnostic est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Le riz offert par la Chine apporte un soulagement aux ménages vulnérables au Cameroun (REPORTAGE)
data.description: © DR A l'aube, dans le quartier de Mbende, à Limbe, ville balnéaire de la région du Sud-Ouest du Cameroun , Vivian Njie, 89 ans, a allumé son feu de bois. Ce matin-là, la marmite posée dessus n'était pas vide. A l'intérieur, du riz blanc à grains longs, offert par la Chine quelques semaines plus tôt, mijotait doucement. "Avant, nous faisions cuire une petite quantité de riz et la répartissions dans cinq assiettes", a raconté cette grand-mère de 15 petits-enfants en remuant une grande marmite destinée aux 19 personnes de son foyer. "Aujourd'hui, mes petits-enfants mangeront jusqu'à ce qu'ils disent : 'Je suis rassasié'. Rien que cela, c'est déjà une tranquillité". Depuis près d'une décennie, les régions anglophones du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest du Cameroun sont confrontées à un conflit armé séparatiste. Des exploitations agricoles ont été abandonnées, l'accès aux marchés est devenu dangereux et les superficies cultivées ont diminué de 20 à 40% dans les zones les plus touchées, entraînant une hausse des prix des denrées alimentaires. Début 2026, les agences humanitaires estimaient que 2,9 millions de personnes au Cameroun , dont 1,5 million d'enfants, avaient besoin d'aide. C'est dans ce contexte que l'aide de la Chine est arrivée. En juin, le Cameroun a reçu de la Chine un don qui comprenait 1.630 tonnes de riz et 880 tonnes de blé destinées aux régions touchées par le conflit. A ce jour, 9.000 sacs de riz ont été acheminés à Buea, chef-lieu de la région du Sud-Ouest, où leur distribution a déjà commencé. Quelque 10.700 autres sacs ont été envoyés à Bamenda pour être distribués dans la région du Nord-Ouest. A Limbe, le maire, Paul Efome Ngalle, a supervisé la remise du riz aux responsables communautaires. Il a déclaré que cette aide arrivait à un moment où la ville était "poussée à ses limites". "Ce don de riz de la Chine n'est pas seulement de la nourriture. C'est de la solidarité. De nombreux groupes vulnérables de notre commune ont réellement bénéficié de cette aide", a-t-il ajouté. Dans un point de distribution à Buea, des familles faisaient la queue avec leurs cartes de rationnement. Chaque ménage a reçu du riz. James Nkemasong, 48 ans, a fui son village dans le département de la Lebialem il y a deux ans avec sa femme et leurs cinq enfants. Il loue aujourd'hui une seule pièce à Buea. "Ce riz nous nourrira pendant des semaines", dit-il en chargeant un sac de 25 kilos sur son épaule. "La situation a été vraiment difficile pour moi et ma famille. Nous avons à peine trois repas par jour. Mais ce riz nous a apporté un soulagement". Un sentiment partagé à Muyuka, une autre ville du Sud-Ouest, où Judith Mbah, 38 ans, cuisine pour 12 déplacés. "Le riz de Chine est tendre et ne consomme pas beaucoup de bois de chauffage", a-t-elle expliqué. "Nous le mélangeons avec des haricots et un peu d'huile. Les enfants l'appellent 'le riz délicieux' et en demandent tous les jours". A son arrivée à Limbe, le riz n'était pas destiné uniquement aux personnes déplacées par le conflit. Il devait aussi bénéficier à tous ceux qui n'avaient plus rien. Début août, de fortes pluies se sont abattues sur cette ville côtière située au pied du mont Cameroun. Les eaux de ruissellement ont dévalé les pentes sans pouvoir s'évacuer. Des quartiers ont été inondés et des glissements de terrain ont détruit des habitations. Trois personnes ont perdu la vie. Pour une communauté déjà éprouvée par les déplacements liés au conflit séparatiste, les inondations ont constitué une nouvelle crise : elles ont entraîné non seulement des pertes de logements, mais aussi des pertes de nourriture. John Molua a perdu une grande partie de ses biens dans les inondations. "La pluie continue de tomber. Mais ce riz nous a apporté de la stabilité et de l'espoir pour plusieurs semaines. Le conseiller économique et commercial de l'ambassade de Chine au Cameroun , Xiao Guofeng, a indiqué que ce don faisait partie des dix actions concrètes annoncées lors du sommet du Forum sur la coopération sino-africaine à Beijing en 2024. "Ce don de denrées alimentaires est un exemple concret de l'amitié entre la Chine et le Cameroun. Il incarne la politique de la Chine à l'égard de l'Afrique, fondée sur les principes de sincérité, de solidarité, d'amitié et de franchise, ainsi que sur une bonne compréhension de l'amitié et des intérêts communs", a-t-il déclaré. Le maire de Limbe, M. Ngalle, a souligné que ce geste témoignait de plus de 55 ans de coopération entre le Cameroun et la Chine. "Ce geste approfondit non seulement les relations entre les nations, mais aussi les relations entre les citoyens, les relations entre les peuples", a-t-il déclaré. A Buea et Limbe, où les conflits et les inondations ont durement éprouvé les familles, ces sacs de riz remplissent ainsi leur vocation première : aider les populations à tenir bon. De retour à Mbende, Njie a servi le riz. Ses petits-enfants ont mangé rapidement avant de sortir jouer. Elle les a regardés en souriant. Dans une région qui a connu tant de souffrances, une assiette de riz fumante ravive l'espoir, bol après bol. data.title: Cameroun : des partis politiques en ordre de bataille contre les féminicides
data.description: © DR Face à la montée des assassinats ciblant les femmes au Cameroun, les partis politiques prennent la défense de la cause féminine et demandent des sanctions exemplaires contre les auteurs de tels crimes. En huit mois, plus de 60 femmes ont été froidement tuées au Cameroun. Face au phénomène qui s'accroît, l’inquiétude est générale et l'indignation s'empare de la sphère politique nationale. Préoccupés par la récurrence des feminicides au Cameroun, le Mouvement patriotiques pour la prospérité du peuple (MP3), le Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun (MRC), le Parti camerounais pour la réconciliation nationale (PCRN), le Social Democratic Front (SDF) et bien d'autres érigent un front pour protéger et défendre les femmes en danger. Devant des vies arrachées, des familles brisées, des enfants privées de leurs mères, «le silence et l'inaction» ne sont plus une réponse. Le MP3 propose la protection des femmes en danger, une sanction sévère contre les agresseurs et la prévention de la violence par l'éducation des enfants pour briser le cycle de la violence. Dans une communication en date du 26 août 2026, le bureau politique du parti s'indigne de la banalisation de la violence sur les femmes et interpelle l'État qui n'accorde pas la priorité à ce sujet. L'interpellation des pouvoirs publics, c'est aussi ce que fait le MRC en condamnant fermement « l'hémorragie silencieuse » liée aux feminicides domestiques. Le parti dénonce le silence coupable des autorités, l'indifférence générale, ainsi que la banalisation des actes criminels. Dans une sortie en date du 26 août dernier et signée du secrétaire général adjoint Roger Justin Noah, la formation politique plaide pour des sanctions plus lourdes contre les auteurs de tels assassinats. Et appelle les communautés à développer la vigilance, à dénoncer le moindre fait suspect. « La répression qui jette l'effroi », qui dissuade. C'est le levier qu'il faut actionner d'après le PCRN pour mettre fin à ce phénomène insupportable marqué par des coups, violences et la barbarie sur les femmes. « Aucune colère, aucune jalousie, aucune humiliation, aucune dispute ne donne le droit de frapper ou de tuer », souligne le député Cabral Libii qui insiste pour dire non à la banalisation de la violence. La mise en œuvre des propositions ainsi faites dépend pour la plupart de la volonté de ceux qui tiennent le pouvoir. Mais, d'après le Social Democratic Front, les dirigeants actuels gardent le silence face aux propositions de changer la situation. Dans une déclaration signée de Madeleine Haoua, coordonnatrice nationale des femmes socialistes, le parti rappelle avoir soumis à l'Assemblée nationale des propositions de loi visant à lutter contre les féminicides et autres violences sur els femmes et les enfants. Mais, le Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais, parti majoritaire au Parlement brille par le silence sur ces textes. N'ayant pas la majorité pour décider, le parti de Joshua Osih n'a pu faire que des propositions et se remettre à la volonté de ceux qui ont le pouvoir de décider. De manière collective, les partis d'opposition militent pour des sanctions lourdes contre les agresseurs, appellent les autorités à l'action et les communautés à la vigilance. La mise en œuvre de l'ensemble des solutions peut conduire à résoudre de manière durable l'équation difficile. Cet article Cameroun : des partis politiques en ordre de bataille contre les féminicides est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Félix Tshisekedi exclut l’AFC-M23 du dialogue national inclusif
data.description: Au cours de son adresse à la nation, jeudi 27 août 2026, le président Félix Tshisekedi a clarifiée les contours du dialogue national inclusif qu’il a initié récemment. Tous ceux qui ont pris les armes contré l’ordre constitutionnel établi en RDC ne participeront pas à ces assis, a-t-il martelé. Nul ne sera exclu en raison de ses opinions, de ses critiques, de son appartenance politique, de son origine provinciale, de sa langue, de son ethnie ou de sa religion, a assuré le chef de l’Etat.

data.title: Antonio Guterres mobilise la communauté internationale contre Ebola en RDC
data.description: L’épidémie d’Ebola continue de progresser en RDC, avec plus de 5 700 cas et 2 700 morts depuis sa déclaration officielle il y a trois. data.title: Roads Ministry moves to ease payment bottlenecks affecting consultants
data.description:
The Ministry of Roads and Highways says it is taking steps to address payment-related bottlenecks that have affected consultants working on road projects.

The assurance was given during an engagement between the Ministry, the Ghana Institution of Engineering (GhIE), the Engineering Council and the Ghana Consulting Engineers Association (GCEA) in Accra on Wednesday, August 26, 2026.

The meeting focused on challenges confronting Ghana’s road sector, including delays in project execution, rising construction costs, outstanding payments and financial pressures affecting contractors and consultants.

data.title: Values, disciplined execution key to effective African leadership – Ato Coleman, IMANI
data.description:
Senior Fellow at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Ato Coleman, has called for a shift in how leadership and public policy are approached in Africa, arguing that technical competence alone cannot deliver sustainable and inclusive development.

He said effective leadership must be rooted in personal values, emotional intelligence, stakeholder engagement and disciplined execution.

Speaking at SYPALA 2026 on the topic “What are the leadership, skills and policy priorities needed to position Africa for inclusive and resilient growth,” Mr Coleman said leaders must first develop a strong understanding of the values that guide their decisions before attempting to influence others or implement public policies.

data.title: AG inaugurates 11-member committee to implement Ghana’s proposed constitutional reforms
data.description:
Attorney General (AG) and Minister of Justice, Dr Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, has inaugurated an 11-member Constitution Review Implementation Committee (CRIC) to begin work on proposals for the review of Ghana’s 1992 Constitution.

The inauguration follows the government’s release of its position paper on recommendations contained in the report of the Constitution Review Committee chaired by Professor H. Kwesi Prempeh.

The new committee has been tasked with examining the government’s position paper alongside the recommendations of the Constitution Review Committee and developing a comprehensive framework for implementing the proposals.

data.title: Sir Sam Jonah says Nigerian state agencies subjected his real estate investment to ‘sustained harassment’
data.description:
Ghanaian business leader Sir Sam Jonah has disclosed that a significant real estate investment he made in Nigeria has been subjected to what he describes as “sustained harassment” by state agencies.

He said Ghanaian workers at the project site had also experienced treatment similar to scenes of xenophobic attacks that have been condemned elsewhere on the continent.

Sir Sam Jonah made the disclosure while delivering the keynote address at the Global Business Forum – Ghana Edition on Friday, August 28, 2026.

data.title: ‘Africa exports its savings and imports expensive capital’ – Sir Sam Jonah
data.description:
Ghanaian business leader Sir Sam Jonah has challenged African institutional investors to put more of their capital to work on the continent, warning that Africa is caught in a cycle of exporting its savings while borrowing expensive capital from abroad.

He said the situation was widening the continent’s infrastructure financing gap while leaving promising African businesses struggling to access long-term funding.

Delivering the keynote address at the Global Business Forum – Ghana Edition on Friday, August 28, Sir Sam Jonah described the situation as Africa’s “great paradox”.
